ref_file_title: GGM84 - On the Cryptographic Applications of Random Functions
authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
note: cryptobib C:GolGolMic84 (CRYPTO 1984, LNCS 196, pp. 276-288, doi 10.1007/3-540-39568-7_22). Springer chapter page (via WebSearch snippet) lists among the paper's applications 'constructing deterministic, memoryless authentication schemes which are provably secure against chosen message attack' — i.e. the PRF-based MAC. Extended abstract; distinct from the JACM paper GGM86 (PRF from PRG), which the wiki already has. eprint.iacr.org, arxiv.org, dblp.org, link.springer.com, iacr.org, par.nsf.gov and author sites are egress-blocked this session; bibliographic data verified against vendor/cryptobib and WebSearch result snippets.

ref_file_title: GW11 - Separating Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments From All Falsifiable Assumptions
note: cryptobib STOC:GenWic11 (STOC 2011, pp. 99-108, DOI 10.1145/1993636.1993651); ePrint 2010/610. Abstract verified verbatim via the Microsoft Research mirror: 'black-box reductions cannot be used to prove the security of any SNARG construction based on any falsifiable cryptographic assumption ... extends to designated verifier SNARGs ... and slightly succinct SNARGs, whose size is only required to be sub-linear in the statement and witness size.' The 'sub-exponentially hard subset-membership problem' qualifier is from the paper's main theorem, not its abstract; the paper text could not be fetched (eprint, ACM DL blocked). WW24's abstract snippet independently reads GW11 as requiring sub-exponential hardness.
